text: صباح الخير, سيدي! كل سنه وانتا طيب.

judge_v1.note: انتا is the Egyptian/colloquial shape of the 2ms pronoun أنتَ, and كل سنة وانتا طيب is the spoken festive formula; the MSA equivalent everyone writes is كل عام وأنت بخير, so the row need not be retired. Separately for the spelling pass (not register): سنه written with ه for ة, and a Latin comma after صباح الخير.

judge_v2.msa: صباح الخير، سيدي! كل عام وأنت بخير.
judge_v2.note: انتا is the Egyptian colloquial pronoun for أنت, and كل سنة وانتا طيب is the spoken form of the greeting; the MSA formula is كل عام وأنت بخير, so the meaning survives the rewrite and the row need not be retired. Separately, for the spelling pass: سنه should be سنة (ta marbuta) and the Latin comma should be the Arabic ، — neither is register.

reference.note: وانتا is the colloquial pronoun أنت written with the dialect final vowel (Egyptian enta); MSA writes وأنت. The greeting formula itself is not dialect-only — كل عام وأنت بخير is standard written Arabic — so it rewrites rather than retires. Two non-register faults logged for their own passes: سنه for سنة (ة/ه, orthography, not counted as evidence) and the ASCII comma. The English 'A merry Christmas to you!' is not a translation of the Arabic seasonal formula; that is a translation-fidelity item.

text: لا أعلم ما تخطط له، لكني سأمنعك بالقيام به.

judge_v1.note: MSA register throughout. بالقيام is بـ + a noun (القيام), i.e. the preposition, not the dialect b-imperfect. There is a grammar slip for the grammar pass, not this one: منع governs من, so سأمنعك من القيام به.

judge_v2.note: MSA register throughout; بالقيام is the preposition بـ on a noun, not a b-imperfect. One grammar point for a different pass: منع governs من, so سأمنعك من القيام به rather than بالقيام به.

reference.note: Register is MSA: بالقيام is بـ + noun (the preposition), the explicit non-tell, not a b-imperfect; لكني and سأمنعك are MSA. Separate defect for the grammar pass, not this one: the verb governs من, so سأمنعك من القيام به, and the English 'I won't let you' is weaker than 'I will prevent you'.

text: ليس لدي رغبة في الخروج الليلة فحسب.

judge_v2.note: Clean MSA lexis and syntax. فحسب sits oddly at the end for the English 'just', but that is a style question, not register.

reference.note: MSA lexis and syntax. فحسب is a formal MSA particle; its clause-final placement here renders the English 'just' a little loosely, which is style, not register.

text: هناك سبيلين فقط للخروج من هذا المنزل.

judge_v1.note: MSA register. The only fault is case, not register: after هناك the dual should be nominative سبيلان, not سبيلين — send to the grammar pass, not the register fix.

judge_v2.note: MSA register; no dialect word or dialect morphology. The case of the dual after هناك should be nominative — هناك سبيلان فقط — which is an iʿrab slip for the grammar pass, not a colloquial form.

reference.note: No dialect lexeme and no dialect morphology from the §1.2 list. The one fault is iʿrāb: after هناك the dual is nominative, هناك سبيلان فقط. I deliberately did not file this as morphology — سبيلين is a real MSA form in the wrong case, and the programme counts case endings only where the drill's point is the ending. A reviewer who reads the oblique-invariant dual as colloquial interference would disagree, so the confidence is held down; the fix belongs to the grammar pass.

judge_v1.note: في الواقع and منطقي بالكامل are MSA; بالكامل is بـ + noun, the preposition. Only oddity is punctuation for the spelling pass: a Latin comma instead of the Arabic ،.

text: لا أحد من زملائي يعيشون بالقرب من هنا.

judge_v2.note: MSA register. Agreement slip for the grammar pass: لا أحد takes a singular verb, يعيش not يعيشون.

text: يتمتع والدي بخبرة كبيرة في الحياة ، وأنا دائمًا أتبع نصيحته.

reference.note: MSA: يتمتع بخبرة, أتبع نصيحته; بخبرة is بـ + noun. Tashkeel on دائمًا is optional. Cosmetic only: a space before the comma (الحياة ،).

text: أسمح لك بالذهاب إلى هناك إذا أردت.

text: إذا قمت بتغيير الخطة، فيجب عليك أن تعلم أعضاء الفريق بالتغييرات.

judge_v2.note: Clean MSA conditional with إذا and the fa- of the apodosis. قمت بتغيير and بالتغييرات are بـ on nouns.

text: مع انني كنت جالساً تحت الشمس، ولكن كنت أشعر بالبرد.

judge_v2.note: MSA lexis and morphology; nothing dialectal. Spelling for the spelling pass: انني is missing its hamza — إنني (مع أنني). Style note for another pass: مع أن … ولكن is doubled; MSA press would write مع أنني كنت جالسًا تحت الشمس، إلا أنني كنت أشعر بالبرد.

reference.note: No dialect lexeme or morphology; بالبرد is بـ + noun and جالساً is a correct MSA accusative ḥāl. Two non-register faults: انني is missing its hamza (مع أنني), and مع أن … ولكن doubles the concessive — MSA writes مع أنني كنت جالسًا تحت الشمس، إلا أنني كنت أشعر بالبرد. judge_v2.note: Clean MSA: كي + subjunctive, تلحق بـ. بسرعة and بالآخرين are بـ on nouns, not b-imperfects.

reference.note: MSA: مشت بسرعة كي + subjunctive تلحق بالآخرين. Both بـ forms are prepositions on nouns, the verified non-tell, not b-imperfects.

judge_v1.note: Clean MSA. Passive وُلد plus a transliterated proper name.

text: شفيت جروح مصاص الدماء في الحين.

judge_v1.note: MSA, despite containing الحين. في الحين is the standard temporal phrase 'at once/immediately', which the English 'instantly' confirms; it is not the Gulf الحين meaning 'now'. على الفور or في الحال would be the more frequent modern press choice, but that is style, not register. شفيت is the passive شُفِيت with the tashkeel omitted (folded).

judge_v2.note: في الحين here is the MSA/literary prepositional idiom 'at once, immediately', not the Gulf adverb الحين meaning 'now' (which stands alone, الحين أروح). Same exemption shape as بين الحين والآخر. Style note only: في الحال or على الفور is the commoner press choice. Passive شُفيت جروحُ is fine MSA.

reference.note: Deliberate non-tell check on في الحين. الحين is a Gulf/Iraqi tell ONLY in its dialect sense 'now'; §1.1 already records بين الحين والآخر as a verified false alarm, establishing that الحين inside an MSA idiom is not a tell. Here the phrase is في الحين 'at once, forthwith' — the MSA/literary idiom — and the translation ('instantly') plus the perfective شفيت force that reading, not 'now'. Under the rule that an ordinary MSA word stays MSA unless the sentence forces the dialect reading, this is MSA. Reviewers may prefer على الفور/في الحال as commoner press style, and التأمت over شفيت for wounds; both are style edits outside this pass. Flagged at lower confidence because this is a near neighbour of a real tell and worth a second eye.

judge_v1.note: Clean MSA. بالإقلاع is بـ + verbal noun, the preposition governed by نصح, not a b-imperfect.

judge_v2.note: Textbook MSA: نصح بـ + الإقلاع عن التدخين. بالإقلاع is بـ on a noun.

reference.note: Q1-Q5 clean. VSO نصحني الطبيب, and أقلع عن التدخين is the standard MSA press collocation for giving up smoking. Nothing colloquial in lexeme, morphology, orthography or period.

judge_v1.note: Clean MSA. كمان here is the violin — the listed non-tell — not Levantine كمان 'also'; تعزف على confirms the instrument reading. بمهارة is بـ + noun.

judge_v2.note: الكمان is the instrument 'violin', on the verified not-a-tell list, not Levantine كمان 'also' — it takes the article and follows تعزف على. بمهارة is بـ on a noun. MSA.

reference.note: Non-tell, checked explicitly: كمان here is الكمان 'the violin' — the exact false alarm §1.1 lists as verified — not Levantine كمان 'also'. The definite article and the governing collocation تعزف على (to play an instrument) make the violin reading the only possible one. MSA throughout; do not touch.

text: يجب عليهم حل النزاعات بين الدول.

judge_v1.note: Clean MSA. دول here is the plural of دولة ('states'), the listed non-tell, not the Egyptian demonstrative.

judge_v2.note: الدول is the plural of دولة 'states', on the verified not-a-tell list, not Egyptian دول 'these'; it is definite and governed by بين. MSA.

reference.note: Non-tell, checked explicitly: الدول here is the MSA plural 'states/nations' — §1.1 lists دول (states) as a verified false alarm — not Egyptian دول 'these'. It is definite and governed by بين, so the demonstrative reading is impossible. يجب على + maṣdar (حل) is ordinary MSA.

judge_v1.note: Clean MSA. لدي + noun is the standard possessive construction.

judge_v2.note: لدي + شكوك is MSA (the dialect equivalent would be عندي شكوك). Clean.

judge_v1.note: بكرة is used here in its dialect sense 'tomorrow' (the English confirms it), which is Egyptian — Levantine بكرا is the same word — not the MSA بكرة 'ball/early morning'. MSA is غدًا. The register fix is that one word; I also wrote ستلقي for ستقلي, which looks like a letter-transposition typo for 'you will deliver', and restored the accusative tanwin on خطابًا — both spelling, not register, so the minimal register-only rewrite is ستقلي خطاب غدًا، أليس كذلك؟ if you prefer it.

judge_v2.note: بكرة is used here in its Egyptian sense 'tomorrow' — the translation confirms it — not the exempt senses 'ball' or 'early morning'. Replaced with غداً and nothing else touched. Two non-register defects to pass on separately: ستقلي is a letter-transposition typo for ستُلقي, and خطاب wants the accusative خطاباً as an indefinite object.

reference.note: Stops at Q2. بكرة for 'tomorrow' is an Egyptian lexeme (§1.1; MSA غدًا) and ar.md's drill standards name it explicitly. Ran the non-tell test anyway: بكرة does exist in MSA as بَكْرة 'pulley/reel' and بُكْرَة 'early morning', but the temporal adverbial slot and the translation force the Egyptian 'tomorrow' sense, so the dialect reading is the one the sentence carries. Two further faults fixed in the rewrite but NOT the basis of the verdict: ستقلي is a typo for ستُلقي, and خطاب lacks the accusative خطابًا. text: نحن جميعا مهاجرين, قد لا نكون الأشخاص الأوائل, ولكن حتما من خلال أقاربنا أو أجدادنا.

judge_v1.note: Routing to a human. The vocabulary and syntax are MSA throughout and there is no listed tell; the one problem is مهاجرين as the predicate of نحن, where MSA requires the nominative sound plural مهاجرون. Two defensible readings: (a) a plain iʿrab slip inside otherwise MSA prose, which would make this 'msa', or (b) dialect influence, since the dialects have collapsed the sound masculine plural onto the -in form. It is not folded orthography — مهاجرون vs مهاجرين differs in the written letters, not in tashkeel. The rewrite above is the nominative fix plus Arabic commas for the Latin ones.

judge_v2.note: Lexicon and syntax are MSA (قد لا نكون, حتماً, من خلال, أقاربنا أو أجدادنا) with no dialect lexeme or dialect morphology. The real defect is إعراب: the predicate of نحن should be nominative مهاجرون, not مهاجرين — a case-ending slip (possibly colloquial-influenced), which is not one of the listed register tells, so I have not called it dialect. Also for the spelling pass: Latin commas ',' for Arabic '،', and جميعا/حتما unmarked for the accusative alif tanwin.

reference.note: Genuinely wants a second opinion, which is why it is unsure rather than a call either way. Everything else passes: قد لا نكون, الأشخاص الأوائل, حتمًا, من خلال are all MSA lexemes and MSA grammar. The single issue is مهاجرين as the predicate of a verbless sentence, where MSA requires nominative مهاجرون. Two defensible readings: (a) register — levelling the sound masculine plural to -īn in every case is exactly the dialect morphology §1.2 says word lists never catch, and unlike a dropped ending it is written into the consonantal skeleton and survives normalization; (b) not register — §1.2 qualifies case endings with 'only where the drill's point is the ending', and a nominative slip in otherwise clean MSA is the sort of thing a native writes carelessly, which would put it in the grammar/spelling pass. It is also pan-dialectal, so no variety can be named. Reviewer decides which pass owns it; the rewrite above is correct either way. Separately, ASCII ',' for '،' twice, and the sentence is translationese — both for other passes.

text: مدير المشروع الجديد هو ابن عم زوجتي، وهذا ما أزعج الموظفين.

judge_v2.note: Three listed non-tells appear together and none is a tell here: هو is the MSA pronoun/copula, عم in ابن عم is 'paternal uncle' (hence 'my wife's cousin'), and فين occurs only as a substring of الموظفين 'the employees'. Judged as whole words in context, this is plain MSA.

text: لا تقل لجدتي إنني رسبت، فأنا أريد أن أخبرها بنفسي.

text: عمّ تعتذر الآن وقد جرحت أمك أمام الضيوف كلهم؟

text: جارتي مجنونة بكرة القدم، تحفظ أسماء اللاعبين وأرقام قمصانهم.

text: يعمل جاري خادمًا في فندق قديم، ويعود إلى بيته بعد منتصف الليل.

judge_v1.note: خادمًا is an MSA ḥāl accusative; يعمل and يعود are plain imperfects with no بـ or عم progressive marker.

text: ربما كنتُ قاسيًا في كلامي أمس، وأنا نادم منذ ذلك الحين.

text: يقول الجيران إن روح المرأة العجوز تتجول ليلا في الطاحونة المهجورة.

judge_v1.note: إنّ + noun clause, تتجول, الطاحونة المهجورة — all MSA. ليلا is written without the tanwīn mark, which is undiacritised spelling, not register.

text: لم أشعر بالراحة في بيتنا الجديد حتى علقت أمي صور القرية على الجدران.

judge_v1.note: لم + jussive negation and حتى + perfect are MSA. علقت, الجدران and القرية are all standard vocabulary.

judge_v2.note: بالراحة and بيتنا are both بـ + noun (preposition and possessed noun), never the b-imperfect. لم أشعر … حتى + perfect is MSA.

text: يبيع عم سعيد الشاي أمام محطة القطار منذ ثلاثين سنة.

text: سافر خالي إلى أمريكا قبل عشرين عاماً ولم يزر القرية منذ ذلك الحين.

judge_v2.note: منذ ذلك الحين again — the MSA 'since then', not Gulf الحين 'now'. خالي (maternal uncle), قبل عشرين عاماً and لم + jussive يزر are all standard.

judge_v2.note: بسلسلة is بـ + noun (instrumental preposition), not the b-imperfect. قبل أن + subjunctive يغادر is MSA.

text: وجدتُ متعة غريبة في ترتيب المطبخ ليلاً بينما ينام البيت كله.

text: لم أقابل في حياتي شخصًا أكرم من جارنا أبي محمود.

judge_v2.note: MSA. بطاقة زيارة is the standard term for a visiting/business card; تحمل كتابات دينية is press register.

reference.note: كانت ... تحمل is the MSA past-continuous frame and بطاقة زيارة is the MSA term for a visiting/business card (the colloquial كرت is absent). دينيّة carries shadda only — tashkeel is not graded.

text: لديها أفكار مضحكة حول كيفية إدارة شركة.

judge_v1.note: لديها, حول كيفية and the verbal noun إدارة are all MSA.

judge_v2.note: MSA. لديها, كيفية إدارة — all standard written forms.

reference.note: لديها, حول كيفية + verbal noun and إدارة شركة are all MSA press phrasing. No tells.

judge_v1.note: شكل is an MSA noun ('form, appearance') and شكلها فاتن is a well-formed MSA nominal sentence, so no dialect lexeme or dialect morphology is present. Flagging only that شكلها + predicate as a way of saying 'she looks' has a colloquial flavour; press register would write تبدو فاتنةً في ذلك الفستان. Style, not register — left as MSA.

judge_v2.note: Read as a nominal sentence 'her appearance is charming', which is plain MSA: شكل is an MSA noun and فاتن an MSA adjective. This is NOT the Levantine/Egyptian evidential شكلها ('it seems she...'), which takes a state predicate. Press register would prefer تبدو فاتنة في ذلك الفستان, but that is a style preference, not a dialect tell, and the rule against false alarms applies.

reference.note: Checked the first reaction against the non-tells rule: شكل is an ordinary MSA noun and this is a well-formed nominal sentence, 'her appearance is charming'. The colloquial evidential شكلها ('it seems that she…') is a different reading and the sentence does not force it. ذلك الفستان has the demonstrative BEFORE the noun, i.e. MSA order. Press would write تبدو فاتنة في ذلك الفستان — a style preference, not a register defect. Low confidence because a second reviewer may judge the شكلها + adjective frame colloquial-flavoured.

judge_v1.note: سكارى is the MSA broken plural of سكران; sentence is MSA. Separately for the translation pass: the Arabic means 'they are all drunk', not 'they all drank'.

judge_v2.note: The Arabic is MSA: سكارى is the standard broken plural of سكران, and كلهم سكارى is a well-formed nominal sentence meaning 'they are all drunk'. Separately, the English translation 'They all drank' does not match the Arabic (it renders a verb, not the adjectival predicate) — a translation-layer defect for another pass, not a register one.

reference.note: سكارى is the ordinary MSA broken plural of سكران; its Qurʾanic attestation does not make it archaic, since MSA uses it productively, so not 'classical' either. Separate defect for another pass: the English 'They all drank' does not match كلهم سكارى ('they are all drunk') — a translation-accuracy item, not register.

judge_v1.note: هو is the MSA pronoun (verified non-tell); ليس + accusative predicate is MSA. غيورا written without the alif-tanwin mark is spelling only.

judge_v2.note: MSA. هو is on the verified not-a-tell list; ليس + accusative غيورا is standard.

reference.note: هو is on the verified non-tells list. Negation is ليس with an accusative خبر (غيوراً), i.e. the MSA pattern, not مش or ما…ش.

judge_v1.note: البارحة is MSA for 'yesterday/last night'; no dialect form (not مبارح/إمبارح).

judge_v2.note: MSA. البارحة is a standard fusha adverb for 'yesterday/last night', current in written Arabic; أمس is commoner in press but both are MSA.

reference.note: البارحة is standard Arabic for 'last night / yesterday' and is not on the tells list (the Levantine form would be مبارح, the Egyptian إمبارح). أمس is the commoner press word — a preference under §1.5, not a register defect. أصلحت is the MSA form IV perfect.

judge_v1.note: من فضلك and the form IV imperative أقفل are MSA; بهدوء is بـ + noun, i.e. the preposition.

judge_v2.note: MSA. أقفل is the form IV imperative; بهدوء is the preposition بـ on a noun, not a b-imperfect.

reference.note: من فضلك is the MSA politeness formula; أقفِل is a correctly formed form IV imperative (أغلق is an equally MSA alternative); بهدوء is بـ + noun, the preposition.

text: اعتاد سامي على حياته المزدوجة إلى حدّ كبير.

judge_v1.note: اعتاد على and إلى حدّ كبير are MSA; the shadda on حدّ is tashkeel, i.e. spelling.

judge_v2.note: MSA. اعتاد على, حياته المزدوجة and إلى حد كبير are all standard written register.

reference.note: اعتاد على and إلى حدّ كبير are both MSA. The English 'too comfortable' renders إلى حد كبير loosely — a translation matter for that pass, not register.

judge_v1.note: No dialect lexeme and no dialect morphology from the list. One grammar slip for the grammar pass, not the register pass: as subject of a nominal sentence the dual should be nominative يداها, not oblique يديها (يداها ناعمتان جدًا). Oblique-dual generalisation is also a colloquial habit, so a reviewer may want to see this one.

judge_v2.note: Subject of a nominal sentence must be nominative dual يداها; يديها is the oblique dual, and the invariant oblique dual (-ayn in every case) is the colloquial pattern rather than an MSA one. It is not a spelling issue — not final ى/ي, ة/ه, a hamza seat or tashkeel — so the orthography rule does not cover it. Confidence held under the reviewer threshold because an ordinary i'rab slip by an MSA writer would look identical; the fix is the same either way. جدا unvowelled for جدًا is spelling only.

reference.note: Real defect, but not a register one on this programme's rules: as subject of a nominal sentence MSA writes the nominative dual يداها, and يديها is the oblique dual. The predicate ناعمتان is itself a correct nominative dual, so the writer has MSA dual morphology and slipped on one case form — this reads as a case slip rather than the dialects' generalised -ayn dual, and §1.2 flags dual/case endings only where a drill's point IS the ending, which does not apply to a sentence row. Logged for the grammar/typo pass. Confidence deliberately below 0.7: a second reviewer could defensibly read it as dialect morphology, and this item is worth adjudicating.

text: ظرف و طابع بريد من فضلك.

judge_v1.note: MSA. Spelling only: the conjunction waw is written detached with a space ('ظرف و طابع') — it should be attached, وطابع. For the spelling pass.

judge_v2.note: Lexis and grammar are MSA (ظرف وطابع بريد، من فضلك). Only oddity is spelling, for the spelling pass: the conjunction و is written detached with a following space ('ظرف و طابع') where Arabic joins it to the next word — should be 'ظرف وطابع بريد من فضلك.'

reference.note: Vocabulary and grammar are MSA (ظرف, طابع بريد, من فضلك). The only oddity is typographic: the conjunction is detached, 'ظرف و طابع' where Arabic writes وطابع. Spelling, not register — left untouched here and logged for the spelling pass.

text: لا ريب أن للدين مكانة هامة في حياة الناس.

judge_v1.note: لا ريب أن is ordinary MSA press/essay register, not archaic or Qurʾanic; هامة is standard MSA.

judge_v2.note: MSA, formal but current: لا ريب أن is live press and textbook usage, not an archaism, and للدين مكانة هامة is a standard fronted-predicate construction.

reference.note: Considered 'classical' because لا ريب echoes the Qurʾanic لا ريب فيه, and rejected it: لا ريب أن is productive in MSA editorial prose alongside لا شك أن. للدين مكانة is ordinary fronted-predicate MSA, and هامة beside مهمة is accepted press variation.

text: يأكل ياني كل شيء بالبطاطا المقلية.

judge_v1.note: بالبطاطا is بـ + noun, the preposition 'with', not the b-imperfect. بطاطا مقلية is accepted MSA vocabulary.

judge_v2.note: MSA. بالبطاطا is the preposition بـ plus a noun, never the b-imperfect. بطاطا and بطاطس are both accepted regional lexical preferences in pan-Arab MSA and must not be 'fixed'.

reference.note: بالبطاطا is بـ + noun (preposition), explicitly a non-tell, not a b-imperfect. بطاطا vs بطاطس is pan-Arab MSA lexical variation under §1.5 and must not be 'fixed'. المقلية is the MSA passive participle.

judge_v1.note: Standard MSA proverb; بحجر is the preposition بـ on a noun.

judge_v2.note: MSA. أصاب عصفورين بحجر واحد is the standard written form of the proverb; بحجر is the preposition on a noun.

reference.note: MSA proverb (the commoner citation form is ضرب عصفورين بحجر واحد; أصاب is an MSA variant). عصفورين is a correctly formed accusative dual object and بحجر is بـ + noun.

text: يتحول الجليد إلى ماء عندما يذوب.

judge_v1.note: يتحول ... إلى, عندما and يذوب are all MSA.

judge_v2.note: MSA. يتحول ... إلى, عندما, يذوب are all standard written register.

reference.note: Every word MSA; عندما is the MSA temporal conjunction, and the bare imperfects يتحول/يذوب carry the present with no b- prefix.

judge_v1.note: لقد + perfect is MSA press usage; عاد إلى/للواجهة is a standard newspaper collocation.

judge_v2.note: MSA. لقد + perfect and عادت ... للواجهة are ordinary press usage. التنافسات is a licit plural of تنافس (منافسات is commoner) — a lexical-choice matter, not register.

reference.note: عاد إلى/للواجهة is a standard MSA press idiom and لـ for إلى is common journalistic usage; لقد + perfect is MSA. التنافسات as a plural of the verbal noun is slightly unusual next to المنافسات — style, not register.

judge_v1.note: ثرثار is MSA; جداً with tanwin alif is spelling only.

judge_v2.note: MSA. ثرثار is a standard fusha adjective for 'talkative'; جداً is the normal intensifier.

reference.note: ثرثار is the MSA adjective and جداً the MSA intensifier (the dialect intensifiers أوي/كتير/بزاف are absent).

judge_v1.note: Plain MSA throughout: interrogative من, perfect ترك, accusative complement مفتوحة. No dialect lexeme or morphology.

judge_v2.note: Plain MSA: relative مَن + past verb ترك, object الجرة with predicative مفتوحة. No dialect lexeme or morphology; the question word is initial, not final.

reference.note: Q1 complete Arabic. Q2 من/ترك/الجرة/مفتوحة are all ordinary MSA; جرة (clay jar) is MSA lexicon, not a dialect word. Q3 question word fronted, verb-initial — MSA order, not the dialect final-position pattern. Q4-Q5 nothing. Clean.

text: يرجى ملء نموذج طلب الوظيفة المرفق.

judge_v1.note: Formal MSA administrative register (يرجى + verbal noun ملء + المرفق). Exactly the press/textbook register.

judge_v2.note: Formal MSA administrative register (يرجى + masdar ملء, المرفق). Exactly the press/textbook register.

reference.note: Textbook administrative MSA: يرجى + مصدر (ملء), نموذج طلب الوظيفة, participle المرفق. No tell at any layer.

judge_v1.note: MSA: imperfect يعمل with accusative حال محاسبًا. Only oddity is the missing sentence-final full stop, which is punctuation, not register.

judge_v2.note: MSA: verb-initial يعمل with accusative حال محاسبًا. The missing final full stop is typography, not register.

reference.note: MSA throughout; محاسبًا is a correctly accusative complement. Only defect is a missing sentence-final full stop — punctuation, not register or spelling; log for the typography/punctuation pass, not this one.

text: ماذا كنتِ ستفعلينَ لو كُنتِ أصغر بعشر سنين؟

judge_v1.note: MSA conditional لو + كان with the future ستفعلين; feminine addressee vowelled. سنين is the oblique sound plural of سنة and is ordinary MSA after a number (سنوات is the commoner press choice, but both are MSA and neither is a fix).

judge_v2.note: MSA conditional with لو + كان and the ستفعلين future; feminine addressee marked كنتِ/ستفعلينَ. سنين is a standard oblique plural of سنة beside سنوات, not a dialect form.

reference.note: كان + سـ + imperfect is the standard MSA counterfactual ('what would you have done'); سـ is the MSA future, not a ha-/h- prefix. سنين is the MSA (and Classical) genitive plural of سنة and is current in MSA press — not archaic under 1.4 — and عشر سنين is correct reverse-polarity agreement for a feminine counted noun. Partial tashkeel is not graded.

judge_v1.note: MSA: صبّت + dative لي + accusative كأسًا. Written كأساً (tanwin placed before the alif) rather than كأسًا — a tashkeel-placement spelling variant only, which the grader folds.

judge_v2.note: MSA: صبّت لي كأسًا من الشاي, with the accusative tanwin written. Nothing colloquial in lexis or morphology.

reference.note: صبّ 'to pour' and كأس 'glass/cup' are both MSA lexicon; كأساً carries the accusative with its alef. لي is the MSA dative, not a dialect benefactive. Clean.

judge_v1.note: MSA question particle هل with the س- future and accusative predicate of أصبح. No dialect tell.

judge_v2.note: MSA question: هل + سـ future, أصبح taking the accusative predicate دولة ثرية (tanwin unwritten, which is tashkeel only).

reference.note: هل + سـ + أصبح is MSA interrogative and future. الجزائر is the country's name; a Maghrebi referent is not a Maghrebi register, and no واش/بزاف/كاين-type form appears.

judge_v1.note: MSA nominal sentence (نحن + indefinite iḍāfa رؤساء أقسام). The English gloss 'class presidents' does not match رؤساء أقسام ('department heads'), but that is translation accuracy for another pass, not register.

judge_v2.note: MSA nominal sentence. The English gloss 'class presidents' does not match رؤساء أقسام ('department heads'), but that is a translation issue for another pass, not register.

reference.note: Register clean: MSA nominal sentence, رؤساء أقسام a sound MSA iḍāfa. Separately, the translation has drifted — رؤساء أقسام is 'department/section heads', not 'class presidents' (that would be رؤساء الصفوف). Log for the translation pass; out of scope here per §7.

text: أحب تفكيك الاشياء لمعرفة كيفية عملها.

judge_v1.note: MSA throughout (أحب + verbal noun تفكيك, لمعرفة كيفية عملها). Spelling only: الاشياء is written without its hamza, for الأشياء. Hamza seats are spelling, not register — flagging for the spelling pass.

judge_v2.note: MSA lexis and syntax throughout (تفكيك, لمعرفة كيفية عملها). Only oddity is the bare alif in الاشياء, which should be الأشياء — a hamza seat, i.e. spelling, for the orthography pass.

reference.note: Every word and every structure is MSA (أحب + مصدر, لمعرفة كيفية عملها). The sole oddity is the dropped hamza in الاشياء for الأشياء — a hamza seat, explicitly coached-not-failed under §1.3. Filed for the spelling pass; not to be touched under the register pass.

judge_v1.note: No dialect lexeme or morphology: يحبّ is the plain MSA imperfect with no بـ prefix, and الأكل is a legitimate MSA verbal noun also used for 'food'. الطعام or المطبخ المصري would read as higher press register, but الأكل is not a dialect word and must not be 'fixed' as one.

judge_v2.note: No dialect tell: الأكل is the MSA masdar of أكل and is used for 'food' in MSA. Press register would more often write الطعام المصري or المأكولات المصرية, but that is style preference, not a register violation.

reference.note: Checked adversarially because the topic is Egyptian: the topic is not the register. No ب-imperfect (يحبّ is bare, Egyptian would be بيحب), no مش, no post-noun demonstrative. الأكل is an ordinary MSA verbal noun used for 'food' in MSA press (الأكل الصحي) and is not on the tell list; the sentence does not force a dialect reading, so it is MSA by the non-tell rule. الطعام/المطبخ would be a shade more formal — a style preference, not a register fault.

text: تحوّل جسم سامي بواسطة عمليّات جراحيّة لتعديل جنسه.

judge_v1.note: MSA: form V تحوّل, the formal connective بواسطة, and عمليّات جراحيّة with shadda marked. بواسطة is بـ + noun, i.e. the preposition, not a b-imperfect.

judge_v2.note: MSA: بواسطة + عمليات جراحية + purpose lam with masdar تعديل. The بـ in بواسطة is the preposition on a noun, not a b-imperfect.

reference.note: Form V تحوّل, بواسطة, عمليات جراحية, لتعديل جنسه — all MSA press vocabulary and syntax. بواسطة is disliked by some purists in favour of عن طريق but is standard MSA usage; not a register fault.

judge_v1.note: No dialect form: تدين لي is the MSA verb دان/يدين. Strict MSA would govern the sum with بـ and spell it out (تدين لي بستمئة دينار); the bare numeral is syntax/typography, and digit form is explicitly not register.

judge_v2.note: تدين (from دان يدين, to owe) is MSA. The gap is syntax, not register: MSA governs the amount with بـ — تدين لي بستمائة دينار / بـ600 دينار. The digits themselves are folded by the grader.

reference.note: No dialect lexeme or morphology: تدين لي is MSA دان يدين لـ, and ASCII digits are folded under §1.3, not a register matter. The looseness is syntactic — MSA governs the amount with بـ (تدين لي بستمائة دينار), and the bare complement reads as a calque of the English. Note for the syntax/naturalness pass; it is not evidence of any dialect. Singular دينار after 600 is correct.

text: كوكب المريخ يشبه كوكبنا في نواحي عدّة.

judge_v1.note: MSA: يشبه + object, and نواحٍ عدّة is standard press phrasing. Written نواحي rather than the fully inflected نواحٍ — a tanwin/final-ya spelling matter the grader folds, not a register tell.

judge_v2.note: MSA sentence (يشبه, نواحٍ عدة). Only flaw is writing the manqus noun as نواحي where the indefinite genitive should be نواحٍ — a final-ya/tanwin spelling matter for the orthography pass.

reference.note: MSA astronomy register: كوكب المريخ يشبه كوكبنا. في نواحٍ عدة is the fully-pointed form; written نواحي, which is the normal unvocalized manqūṣ spelling in MSA print and falls under the tashkeel-presence class of §1.3 rather than being a defect worth a fix row. Not dialect.

judge_v1.note: MSA: دائمًا ما + imperfect is standard written Arabic, and متأخّرين is the accusative حال. دائماً carries the tanwin before the alif — spelling only.

judge_v2.note: MSA: دائمًا ما + imperfect, with the accusative حال متأخرين. Standard written idiom.

reference.note: دائمًا ما + imperfect is a standard MSA frequency construction, and متأخّرين is a correctly accusative ḥāl. Clean.

judge_v1.note: Simple MSA nominal sentence with a transliterated proper noun. No dialect tell.

judge_v2.note: Simple MSA equational sentence; no dialect copula, demonstrative or negation.

reference.note: Three-word MSA nominal sentence. بيكاسو matched a b-prefix scan mechanically; it is a transliterated proper noun, not a b-imperfect — the §1.2 false-alarm shape exactly.

text: رد ديما: "لا، لتساعدني على شراء هذه البذلة من أرماني. أنا متسخ، ألا تذكر؟"

judge_v1.note: MSA: purposive لـ + subjunctive لتساعدني, demonstrative هذه BEFORE its noun (البذلة), and negative interrogative ألا تذكر — all standard. رد and متسخ are masculine while ديما is usually a woman's name, but that is agreement, not register.

judge_v2.note: MSA throughout: رد, لتساعدني (lam of purpose), شراء, البذلة, ألا تذكر. The gender mismatch between the name ديما and masculine متسخ is a content bug, not a register one.

reference.note: Register is MSA: لـ + subjunctive (لتساعدني), demonstrative BEFORE its noun (هذه البذلة — the dialect pattern would be البذلة دي/هاي), متسخ and ألا تذكر both MSA. Two non-register defects to log elsewhere: gender agreement (رد and متسخ are masculine while ديما is normally a woman's name) and a translation that drops 'so that you help me' and the word 'suit'. Confidence reduced for the garbled quotation, not for any dialect suspicion.

text: لكل إنسان حق التمتع بكافة الحقوق والحريات الواردة في هذا الإعلان، دون أي تمييز، كالتمييز بسبب العنصر أو اللون أو الجنس أو اللغة أو الدين أو الرأي السياسي أو أي رأي آخر، أو الأصل الوطني أو الاجتماعي أو الثروة أو الميلاد أو أي وضع آخر، دون أية تفرقة بين الرجال والنساء.

judge_v1.note: The official Arabic text of UDHR Article 2 — formal MSA legal register (كافة, الواردة, دون أي تمييز). Nothing to change.

judge_v2.note: The official Arabic text of UDHR Article 2 — formal MSA legal register, the high end of الفصحى.

reference.note: The official Arabic text of UDHR Article 2 — the canonical MSA legal register. كافة before its noun is a prescriptivist quibble, not a register fault. The supplied English omits the closing clause دون أية تفرقة بين الرجال والنساء; translation-coverage note only. Length/level may matter to another pass.

text: حاولت تكرارا و مرارا و لم أنجح.

judge_v1.note: MSA lexis and morphology (حاولت, لم أنجح with the jussive). Spelling/typography only: the conjunction و is written detached twice; it should be attached (ومرارًا, ولم). The fixed MSA collocation is usually مرارًا وتكرارًا in that order, which is style, not register.

judge_v2.note: MSA lexis (حاولت، مرارًا وتكرارًا، لم أنجح). Only issues are spacing — و written detached from the following word twice — and the conventional order مرارًا وتكرارًا; neither is register.

reference.note: Lexicon and grammar are MSA (حاولت, لم + jussive أنجح). The only defects are orthographic: the conjunction و is a proclitic and must be attached — ومرارًا, ولم — so this is a spelling row, not a register one. If the spelling pass files detached-waw as typography rather than spelling, re-file it there. Also the fixed MSA idiom is مرارًا وتكرارًا, reversed here — idiom/style, logged separately.

text: الصبي قال ان سيارة الاجرة اختفت في الضباب.

judge_v1.note: MSA sentence (قال إنّ + سيارة الأجرة + اختفت). Spelling only: ان for إنّ and الاجرة for الأجرة — missing hamzas, which the grader folds. For the spelling pass, not a register fix.

judge_v2.note: MSA sentence (سيارة الأجرة اختفت في الضباب). Two hamza-seat omissions only: ان for أنّ and الاجرة for الأجرة — spelling for the orthography pass.

reference.note: سيارة الأجرة is the MSA word for taxi and قال إنّ is the MSA complementiser; fronting الصبي before قال is permitted MSA topicalisation, not dialect word order. The two oddities are dropped hamza seats — ان for إنّ and الاجرة for الأجرة — coached, not failed, under §1.3.

text: سُجِنَ رجل بتهمة العنصرية ، حيث تحدث بشكل معنف ضد المرأة مع سائح فرنسي.

judge_v1.note: MSA news register: passive سُجِنَ, بتهمة (بـ + NOUN, the preposition, not the b-imperfect), حيث, بشكل. Only oddity is the space before the Arabic comma. معنف is an awkward choice for 'abusive' (عنيف/مسيء reads better) but is MSA, not dialect.

judge_v2.note: MSA news register: passive سُجِنَ, بتهمة (بـ on a noun = preposition), حيث + verb. The space before the comma is typography; بشكل معنف is an awkward rendering of 'misogynist tirade' but not colloquial.

reference.note: Register is MSA: passive سُجِنَ with damma marked, بتهمة العنصرية (بـ + noun, a §1.2 non-tell), حيث as a press connective. معنف is a real MSA participle of عنّف 'to rebuke' but is the wrong word here and is most likely a typo for عنيف (بشكل عنيف) — a lexical-choice defect, not a dialect one, so it does not make the row 'dialect'. Also a stray space before the comma, and a translation mismatch (Arabic: spoke violently against women, with a French tourist; English: a tirade against a French tourist). All three go to other passes.

text: كانا يتصافحان بصميمية وكأنهما لم يريا بعضهما لسنوات.

text: كتبتُ اسمي على علبة الطعام حتى لا يأخذها أحد من الثلاجة.

judge_v1.note: Clean MSA. حتى لا + subjunctive is the standard negative-purpose construction, not the ha-/h- future particle — a regex for ح+imperfect matches حتى spuriously. علبة and الثلاجة are both MSA.

judge_v2.note: MSA throughout: حتى لا + subjunctive negative purpose clause, علبة and ثلاجة are standard words.

reference.note: علبة (container/tin) and ثلاجة (fridge) are both ordinary MSA nouns, not dialect items; ثلاجة is the pan-Arab MSA word. حتى لا + subjunctive يأخذها is MSA purpose-negation, not ما…ش or مش. Everyday subject matter but the register is plain MSA press/textbook.

text: يدرّس مارك اللغة الإنجليزية في معهد وسط المدينة منذ ثلاث سنوات.

judge_v1.note: Clean MSA. يدرّس is form II imperfect with no b- prefix; منذ ثلاث سنوات is the standard durative. معهد and وسط المدينة are MSA.

judge_v2.note: MSA. يدرّس (form II, to teach) with منذ ثلاث سنوات is standard. معهد وسط المدينة is a slightly loose indefinite-plus-adjunct construction, but that is style, not register.

reference.note: يدرّس (form II), معهد, منذ ثلاث سنوات are MSA; منذ + perfect-less durative is the MSA way to render an English present perfect continuous. وسط المدينة reads as an adverbial accusative of place (وسطَ المدينة) qualifying معهد — slightly compressed, and a copy editor might prefer معهد في وسط المدينة, but that is style, not register, and nothing on the §1.1–1.4 lists fires.

text: قف مكاني في الطابور دقيقتين حتى أشتري الخبز من الفرن.

judge_v1.note: MSA lexically and morphologically: الطابور (queue) and الفرن (bakery/oven) are both standard, and حتى أشتري is subjunctive purpose, not a future particle. قف مكاني reads slightly spoken — MSA press would more likely write قف في مكاني or احجز لي مكاني — but an omitted preposition with an adverbial accusative is a style point, not a register tell, so no rewrite.

judge_v2.note: MSA imperative قف with حتى + subjunctive. الطابور (queue) and الفرن (bakery/oven) are both standard MSA, not dialect substitutes.

reference.note: Deliberately checked the two words that could trip a false alarm. طابور is an MSA noun (queue/column, Turkish loan long naturalised in MSA press), not on any tell list. فرن is MSA for the oven and, by long-standing extension attested since the classical dictionaries (فرّان = baker), the place bread is baked; المخبز would be the more formal choice but فرن is not a dialect lexeme. قف مكاني is grammatical MSA (مكاني adverbial accusative) though the idiom is spoken-flavoured — MSA prose would more likely write احفظ لي مكاني. Conversational tone in wholly MSA words and morphology is not a register defect under §7, so msa; confidence lowered for the idiom, not for any tell.

text: نام الطفل على وسادة عالية، فاشتكى من ألم في عنقه صباحاً.

judge_v1.note: Clean MSA. فـ + past (فاشتكى) is the standard sequential connector; وسادة, عنق and صباحاً are all MSA. No dialect morphology.

judge_v2.note: MSA. فـ as sequential connector, اشتكى من, adverbial صباحاً. Nothing colloquial.

reference.note: نام, وسادة, اشتكى من ألم, عنق, صباحاً are all MSA in their MSA senses. فـ as a consecutive particle is MSA, not a dialect connector. No dialect morphology; verb-initial clause order throughout.

text: شدّ المحاضر ربطة عنقه قبل أن يدخل قاعة المؤتمر المزدحمة.

judge_v1.note: Clean MSA. ربطة عنق is the standard MSA term for a necktie; قبل أن + subjunctive is textbook. No dialect lexeme or morphology.

judge_v2.note: MSA. ربطة عنق is the standard term for necktie; قبل أن + subjunctive is textbook MSA.

reference.note: ربطة عنق is the standard MSA term for a necktie (كرافتة would have been the colloquial/loan alternative and is absent). شدّ, المحاضر, قاعة المؤتمر, المزدحمة all MSA; قبل أن + subjunctive is the MSA subordinator. Reads like press prose.

text: يتقاضى العمال في السوق أجرهم اليومي مساءً قبل إغلاق المحال.

judge_v1.note: Clean MSA, and the listed non-tell applies: العمال here is the ordinary plural 'workers', not a dialect form. يتقاضى and المحال (plural of محلّ) are MSA; مساءً is correct adverbial accusative.

judge_v2.note: MSA. العمال here is the listed non-tell (workers), and المحال is the standard plural of محل. يتقاضى أجرهم اليومي is press register.

reference.note: عمال is explicitly on the §1.1 non-tells list (a verified tripwire false alarm) and is here the plain MSA plural of عامل. يتقاضى (form VI) is formal MSA for drawing a wage, and the singular verb before the plural subject is correct MSA VSO agreement. المحال is the MSA broken plural of محل. أجرهم اليومي, مساءً, إغلاق all MSA.

text: ملأت رائحة الجيف الطريق الترابي، فأغلقنا نوافذ السيارة بسرعة.

judge_v1.note: Clean MSA. الجيف is the MSA plural of جيفة (carcass). بسرعة is بـ + noun, i.e. the preposition, never the b-imperfect. سيارة is allowed pan-Arab MSA.

judge_v2.note: MSA. الجيف is the standard plural of جيفة (carcass) — literary but in current MSA use, not archaic. الطريق الترابي is ordinary MSA.

reference.note: Considered and rejected classical: جيفة/جيف is a live MSA word (رائحة الجيف appears in current reporting), not Qurʾanic vocabulary displaced from everyday MSA, so §1.4 does not fire. الطريق takes a masculine adjective here, which MSA permits (الطريق is of both genders). ملأت, ترابي, أغلقنا نوافذ السيارة, بسرعة all MSA; سيارة is the pan-Arab form named in §1.5. Strong, literary word choice but the right register.

text: غيرت الشركة سياسة الإجازات، فصار على الموظف أن يطلبها قبل شهر.

judge_v1.note: Clean MSA. Substring trap only: مو appears inside الموظف and is not the Gulf negator. صار is a sister of كان in its MSA 'became' sense, and صار على فلان أن is standard; الإجازات is MSA.

judge_v2.note: MSA. صار as a kāna-sister is standard MSA, not the dialect progressive; على الموظف أن يطلبها is the normal obligation construction.

reference.note: صار as a kāna-sister with على + أن is MSA (أصبح على الموظف أن is the same construction); it is not the Levantine صار progressive. سياسة الإجازات, الموظف, يطلبها all MSA — الموظف is the singular of the الموظفين that the tripwire once flagged for containing فين, a documented non-tell. قبل شهر renders 'a month ahead' a little loosely (MSA would more usually write بشهر or قبل شهر من موعدها), which is a translation-precision point for another pass, not register.

text: المدينة تغيرت كثيرًا، ولم تعد كما تركتها قبل عشر سنوات.

judge_v1.note: Clean MSA. كثيرًا is the MSA adverbial, not Levantine كتير (which would be spelled without the ث). لم تعد + كما is standard negative-perfect syntax.

judge_v2.note: MSA. لم تعد + كما clause and topic-fronted المدينة تغيرت are both standard written Arabic.

reference.note: كثيرًا is the MSA adverb; the Levantine tell would be كتير, which is absent. Topic-fronted المدينة تغيرت is an MSA nominal sentence with a verbal predicate, not dialect SVO. لم تعد + jussive and كما تركتها are both MSA. No post-nominal demonstrative, no b-imperfect.

text: أشعر أنّي خارج الحكاية كلّما تحدّث أصدقائي عن سنوات الجامعة.

judge_v1.note: Clean MSA. كلّما + past is the standard iterative; أنّي is the contracted MSA أنّني, not a dialect form. الحكاية is MSA.

judge_v2.note: MSA. أنّي is the ordinary written contraction of أنني (spelling, not register), and كلّما + past is standard. الحكاية is MSA for story.

reference.note: أشعر أنّي is MSA (أنني is the fuller variant; both are standard, and some editors prefer بأنني — a style preference, not register). حكاية is MSA for a tale. كلّما + perfect is the MSA 'whenever' construction. خارج الحكاية is a transparent metaphor rather than a dialect idiom. Nothing on the tell lists.

text: تخبز أمي الخبز كل جمعة، فتملأ رائحته البيت والدرج معاً.

judge_v1.note: Clean MSA. الدرج for a staircase is standard MSA (the dialects more often use سلّم, but درج is not itself a dialect lexeme). تخبز is a bare imperfect with no b- prefix; معاً is correct adverbial accusative.

judge_v2.note: MSA. الدرج in the sense of stairs/stairwell is standard MSA (دَرَج), and تخبز/رائحته/معاً are all unremarkable.

reference.note: Checked الدرج specifically: دَرَج is the MSA word for steps/stairs, and the stairwell sense is the same sense, so it is an MSA word in its MSA sense even though the usage is regionally coloured (بيت الدرج is the fuller MSA phrase). تخبز, رائحته, معاً all MSA. كل جمعة is elliptical for كل يوم جمعة — compressed but attested in MSA. The translation's 'flat' for البيت is a translation-precision note for another pass, not register.

text: آمل أن يتوقف المطر قبل الغروب حتى ننشر الغسيل على السطح.

judge_v1.note: Clean MSA. حتى ننشر is subjunctive purpose, not a ha- future. الغسيل (washing) and السطح (roof) are both MSA; آمل أن is the standard press-register volitional.

judge_v2.note: MSA. آمل أن + subjunctive, نشر الغسيل and السطح are all standard; no dialect future or negation.

reference.note: آمل أن + subjunctive is MSA (not the dialect بدي/بتمنى pattern). نشر الغسيل is the standard MSA collocation for hanging washing; الغسيل and السطح are both MSA. Everyday scene, MSA throughout.

text: من يقدر على حمل هذه الصناديق وحده يستحق أجرا مضاعفا.

judge_v1.note: Clean MSA. من الشرطية with يقدر/يستحق in the jussive-shaped conditional is ordinary MSA, not the archaic energic. أجرا مضاعفا is written without the tanween mark, which is absence of tashkeel, i.e. spelling and not register.

judge_v2.note: MSA. Conditional من يقدر ... يستحق is classical-flavoured but fully productive in current MSA. أجرا مضاعفا is written without the tanwin marks — tashkeel only, folded by the grader.

reference.note: Conditional من + imperfect: the jussive is invisible in the unvocalised skeleton (يقدر/يستحق are spelled identically in jussive and indicative), so no case-ending defect can be read off the text. صناديق is the MSA broken plural; وحده and مضاعفا are MSA. أجرا مضاعفا writes the accusative tanwin as a bare alif, which is ordinary undiacritised practice, not an error — so not orthography_only.

text: بدا الامتحان سهلا في أوله، ثم جاء السؤال الأخير وأربك الجميع.

judge_v1.note: Clean MSA. بدا (to seem) with accusative predicate سهلا, and أربك, are MSA; the missing tanween on سهلا is unvocalised spelling, not a register signal.

judge_v2.note: MSA. بدا + accusative predicate سهلا and أربك الجميع are standard; the missing tanwin on سهلا is tashkeel, not register.

reference.note: بدا + accusative predicate سهلا is MSA. أربك (form IV) and الجميع are MSA; ثم is the MSA sequencer, not a dialect connector. في أوله is idiomatic MSA. Nothing from §1.1–1.4 present.

text: يعمل خالي مهندسًا على سفينة شحن تنقل الحبوب بين جدة وجيبوتي.

judge_v1.note: Clean MSA, with two substring traps: فين appears inside سفينة (ship), and بين is the MSA preposition 'between' — ba on a noun stem, never the b-imperfect. خالي (maternal uncle) is MSA, as is the listed non-tell عم for the paternal one.

judge_v2.note: MSA. خالي (maternal uncle) is standard MSA, and the relative clause تنقل الحبوب agrees correctly with the indefinite سفينة شحن.

reference.note: خالي is the MSA maternal-uncle term, the same class of word as the عم the non-tells list names as a verified false alarm, and here it is kinship, not the Levantine progressive عم. يعمل مهندسًا is the MSA حال accusative. سفينة شحن, تنقل الحبوب, the place names — all MSA. Proper nouns are not register evidence.

text: كل تفصيل في تلك الليلة ما زال محفورا في ذاكرتي.

judge_v1.note: Clean MSA. ما زال + participle is the standard continuative; تلك is a pre-nominal MSA demonstrative, not a post-nominal dialect one. محفورا lacks the tanween mark, which is spelling only.

judge_v2.note: MSA. ما زال + passive participle محفورا is standard written Arabic; the unwritten tanwin is spelling only.

reference.note: ما زال + accusative predicate محفورا is the MSA construction, correctly case-marked. تلك precedes its noun, so the post-nominal demonstrative tell (§1.2) does not fire. تفصيل in the sense 'a detail' is current MSA press usage (تفصيلة is the alternative). محفور في الذاكرة is an MSA idiom.

text: ما زال أهل الحي يتحدثون عن فعلة الجار الذي أطفأ الحريق بمفرده.

judge_v1.note: Clean MSA. فعلة (a deed) and بمفرده (بـ + noun, the preposition) are MSA; أطفأ keeps its hamza seat. الذي is the MSA relative, not dialect اللي.

judge_v2.note: MSA. فَعْلة (deed) is a standard MSA noun, and بمفرده is the written form for 'on his own'. Nothing dialectal.

reference.note: ما زال + plural verbal predicate يتحدثون is MSA; أهل الحي, الجار, أطفأ الحريق, بمفرده are all MSA. فعلة is an MSA noun of single occurrence, so it passes on register, though its usual connotation is of a deed one disapproves of — applied to a heroic act it is a connotation wobble a style pass might change to صنيع or ما فعله. Logged as style, not register, per §7.

text: شعرت أنني أتحدث إلى حائط كلما شرحت له سبب تأخري.

judge_v1.note: Clean MSA. أتحدث إلى حائط renders the idiom with MSA vocabulary throughout; كلما + past is the standard iterative and تأخري is a plain MSA verbal noun.

judge_v2.note: MSA. أتحدث إلى حائط renders the idiom in standard vocabulary; كلما + past and تأخري are ordinary MSA.

reference.note: شعرت أنني, أتحدث إلى, حائط, كلما شرحت له, سبب تأخري — all MSA lexis and morphology; the bare imperfect أتحدث carries the progressive, exactly as MSA requires, with no بـ or عم prefix. 'Talking to a wall' is rendered with an MSA-transparent image rather than a dialect proverb, so no retire-only idiom problem.

judge_v1.note: عم glossed as 'from what?/about what?' is عَمَّ = عن + ما, ordinary MSA, and is on the verified not-a-tell list; it is not the Levantine progressive marker عم.

judge_v2.note: عمّ here is the MSA contraction of عن + ما ('from what? / about what?'), as in عمّ يتساءلون. Explicitly on the not-a-tell list; the rank of 705 is easily earned by this interrogative plus the homographic عمّ (paternal uncle). Not the Levantine progressive marker عم.

reference.note: POS 'particle' and the gloss 'from what?; about what?' identify this as عَمَّ = عَنْ + مَا, a productive MSA contraction (عمّ تبحث؟ عمّ يتحدثون؟). Not the Levantine progressive عم, which §1.1 pairs with the bare imperfect; §1 also lists عم (uncle) as a verified non-tell. The gloss forces a reading that is MSA under either analysis, so §6 Q2 passes.

judge_v1.note: The gloss is the botanical مُو (meu, Meum athamanticum), a rare plant name in the standard lexicon, not the Gulf/Iraqi negator مو. Judged on the sense given this is MSA; rare enough that a reviewer may want to confirm the entry earns a slot.

judge_v2.note: The gloss names an obscure umbelliferous plant (Meum athamanticum). That botanical sense cannot have earned rank 2917 in a corpus of written Arabic; the count belongs to the Gulf/Iraqi negator مو ('not', e.g. مو زين). The entry is a dialect word wearing an MSA gloss — nothing to rewrite, it should be retired.

reference.note: §6 Q2 fails. مو is the Gulf/Iraqi negator (§1.1); the gloss 'meu, baldmoney (Meum athamanticum)' is the rare MSA botanical homograph, and §2 names this exact row as a dialect entry glossed as its homograph. Nothing ranks a plant name at 2917 — the corpus count is dialect frequency. Fix is retirement to vocab_exclusions.tsv with reason 'dialect' (§4.2), not a gloss rewrite; ليس is what the learner should meet instead.

judge_v1.note: Glossed 'black grape', i.e. وَيْن as recorded in the classical dictionaries, not the Levantine question word وين 'where'. MSA by sense, though obscure; the surface form alone is what makes it look like a tell.

judge_v2.note: وَيْن as 'black grape' is a lexicographers' rarity no newspaper prints; it cannot account for rank 3596. The frequency belongs to the Levantine (also Gulf) interrogative وين 'where'. Retire the entry rather than rewrite it; the MSA interrogative is أين.

reference.note: §6 Q2 fails. وين is the Levantine interrogative 'where' (§1.1, MSA أين); 'black grape' is the rare homograph and §2 names this row explicitly. Same reasoning as مو — a grape variety does not earn rank 3596. Retire rather than regloss (§4.2).

judge_v1.note: The sense given is the verb مَشَّ (to suck the marrow from a bone), root م ش ش — a real MSA lexeme, not the Egyptian negator مش, which is a tell only as a whole word in its dialect sense.

judge_v2.note: مَشَّ 'to suck the marrow from a bone' is a dictionary-only verb and could not earn rank 3794. The count belongs to the Egyptian/Levantine negator مش. Entry should be retired; the MSA negators are ليس / لا / ما.

reference.note: §6 Q2 fails. مش is the Egyptian/Levantine negator (§1.1, MSA ليس/لا); the verb gloss 'to suck the marrow from (a bone)' is the rare dictionary homograph مَشَّ, and §2 names this row. Retire (§4.2). Pan-dialectal in use; filed egyptian per the §1.1 table.

judge_v1.note: خلاص in the sense 'liberation, deliverance, riddance' is explicitly verified MSA; only خلاص used as 'OK/enough' would be the Egyptian tell.

judge_v2.note: خَلاص 'deliverance, liberation, riddance' is an ordinary MSA verbal noun (root خ-ل-ص) and is on the not-a-tell list. The rank is earned by the MSA sense; this is not the colloquial خلاص used as 'OK / that's enough'.

reference.note: Checked against the non-tells before calling anything. §1.1 flags خلاص only 'as "OK"' — the Egyptian discourse particle. This row is the noun خَلاص 'deliverance, salvation, riddance', ordinary MSA (الخلاص من, خلاص الأسرى) and plausible at rank 4072 on its MSA sense alone. Exactly parallel to the listed non-tell خلّص (form II 'to rescue'): same root, MSA sense, not a tell. Unlike مو/وين/مش the gloss here is not a rare homograph.

judge_v1.note: كمان 'violin' is the verified MSA noun; only كمان meaning 'also' would be the Levantine tell.

judge_v2.note: كمان 'violin' is standard MSA and a believable word at rank 4187 — the prompt's own worked example. Not the Levantine كمان 'also'.

reference.note: Named verbatim in the §1 non-tells: 'كمان (violin)'. The gloss is the MSA noun كَمَان, not the Levantine كمان 'also' (MSA أيضًا). §6 Q2 passes.

judge_v1.note: دول glossed 'to internationalize' is the form II verb دوّل, verified MSA; only دول as an Egyptian plural demonstrative ('these') would be a tell.

judge_v2.note: دوّل 'to internationalize' (form II of د-و-ل) is MSA press vocabulary, and the same string is also دُوَل 'states' — both common enough to earn rank 4600. Not the Egyptian demonstrative دول 'these'.

reference.note: POS 'verb' and the gloss 'to internationalize' identify دَوَّل (form II), ordinary MSA press vocabulary (تدويل). Not the Egyptian demonstrative دول 'these' (MSA هؤلاء); §1 also lists دول (states) as a verified non-tell. MSA on either reading of the consonant skeleton.

judge_v1.note: بكرة 'early morning' (بُكْرَة) is verified MSA, as is بكرة 'a ball'; only بكرة meaning 'tomorrow' would be the Egyptian tell.

judge_v2.note: بُكرة 'early morning' is MSA (بُكرةً وأصيلًا), and بَكَرة 'ball/pulley' shares the string — بكرة القدم is football. Explicitly on the not-a-tell list; the rank is earned. Not the Egyptian بكرة 'tomorrow'.

reference.note: Genuinely balanced; wants a second opinion and the corpus tokens. For MSA: بُكْرَة 'early morning' is a real fuṣḥā noun (Wehr; adverbial بُكْرَةً), the gloss states that sense, and بَكَرَة 'pulley, spool' is a second MSA reading — a moderate rank is not absurd. For dialect: بكرة 'tomorrow' is a listed Egyptian/Levantine tell (§1.1, MSA غدًا) and was one of only three confirmed defects in the sentence bank (§2), and §2 warns the frequency file counts dialect. Unlike مو/وين/مش the MSA sense is not a dictionary curiosity, so I will not call a false alarm; unlike خلاص/كمان it is not a verified non-tell either. If a reviewer confirms the corpus tokens are the temporal adverb, retire and the MSA is غدًا; if the botanical/temporal MSA noun, leave the row and send the thin gloss to the definition pass.

judge_v1.note: زين as the form II verb 'to adorn, decorate' is verified MSA; only زين meaning 'good' would be the Gulf/Iraqi tell.

judge_v2.note: زيّن 'to adorn, decorate' is an everyday MSA form II verb and plainly earns rank 5530. Not the Gulf/Iraqi زين 'good'.

reference.note: POS 'verb' with 'to adorn, to decorate' is زَيَّنَ (form II), high-frequency MSA — not the Gulf/Iraqi adjective زين 'good' (§1.1, MSA جيد). Same shape as the listed non-tell خلّص: a form II MSA verb homographic with a dialect word is MSA. Rank 5530 is fully explained by the MSA verb.

judge_v1.note: أوي as the verbal noun of أَوَى (form I) is verified MSA; only أوي as the Egyptian intensifier 'very' would be the tell.

judge_v2.note: أُوِيّ, the verbal noun of أَوَى 'to take shelter', is on the not-a-tell list as ordinary MSA. At a rank as deep as 6432 a low-frequency verbal noun is plausible, so the count need not belong to the Egyptian intensifier أوي 'very'. Flagging the modest confidence: if a reviewer finds the rank is actually driven by the Egyptian adverb, the entry would fall to the same retire path as مو/وين/مش.

reference.note: §6 Q2 fails, though less cleanly than 1–3. أوي is a listed Egyptian tell, the intensifier 'very' (§1.1, MSA جدًا), and among the commonest words in written Egyptian. The gloss is not a meaning at all but a form-of stub, 'verbal noun of أَوَى (form I)' — the signature of a dictionary dump, and أَوْي is not a word MSA text uses at any frequency, let alone rank 6432. That is the §4.2 case: a dialect word the corpus counted, carrying its rare homograph's entry. Fix is retirement, not a gloss rewrite. Lower confidence than مو/وين/مش because §2's hand-checked list does not name this row; a reviewer who disagrees should move it to unsure rather than msa.

judge_v1.note: يلا in the sense 'come on / let's go / hurry up' is the colloquial interjection (from يا الله), pan-dialectal but listed under Egyptian in the tell list. MSA uses هيا, and هيا بنا for 'let's go'. The headword itself is the evidence, so the fix replaces the entry's headword rather than editing around it.

judge_v2.note: Here the headword and the gloss agree, and both are dialect: يلا 'come on, let's go' is a colloquial formula with no MSA homograph to carry the rank. The meaning exists in MSA only as هيّا / هيّا بنا, which is a different headword — substituting it would destroy the frequency entry, so set no rewrite and retire the row.

reference.note: §6 Q2 fails, and unambiguously: the gloss states the dialect sense itself rather than an MSA homograph. يلا is a §1.1 tell (MSA هيا) and §2 names this row among the entries that must be retired. Pan-dialectal in use (Egyptian and Levantine alike); filed egyptian per the §1.1 table. Retire to vocab_exclusions.tsv.

judge_v2.note: ذلك is the MSA far demonstrative and one of the highest-frequency words in written Arabic; rank 12 is exactly right. No dialect reading exists.

judge_v1.note: دائم 'lasting, enduring' is standard MSA, common in news and textbook prose.

judge_v1.note: قادم is the MSA active participle of قدم (coming, next, approaching); routine in news register, e.g. الأسبوع القادم.

judge_v2.note: قادم is an MSA active participle used constantly in news (العام القادم). Shared with the dialects, but MSA in its own right at this rank.

reference.note: قادم is the MSA active participle of قدم, standard in press (الأسبوع القادم). No tell.

judge_v1.note: Headword is spelled أني with word-final ya; the lexical item glossed as 'to tarry, to be tardy' is أنى / أَنِيَ, written with alif maqsura. Word-final ى vs ي is spelling, not register, so this is MSA — passing it to the spelling pass, not the register pass.

judge_v2.note: The string is MSA, so the register answer is msa, but the entry is misfiled: rank 316 belongs to أنَّ + ي = أنّي 'that I', a top-frequency MSA function word, not to the rare verb أَنِيَ 'to tarry'. reference.note: Not a register defect but I want it read by someone. The string أني is not on any tell list; in MSA text it is overwhelmingly أنّي 'that I' (أن + ي), which is plain MSA, and the glossed verb أنى 'to tarry' is a real if literary MSA sense (أنى الأمر, لم يأنِ). Two things a reviewer should see: (a) Iraqi آني 'I' is the same consonant string, so some of this frequency count may be dialect corpus, though Iraqi normally writes the madda; (b) the gloss is the rare-homograph pattern ar.md warns about (مش 'to suck the marrow') — the frequent sense is 'that I'. judge_v2.note: الذين is the MSA masculine plural relative pronoun; rank 323 is squarely earned by the MSA function word.

judge_v1.note: شيئا is the MSA accusative indefinite of شيء; the only deviation is the omitted tanwin mark (شيئًا), which is tashkeel and therefore folded by the grader, not a register signal.

judge_v2.note: شيئا is the MSA accusative indefinite of شيء. The missing tanwin fatha (شيئًا) is tashkeel, i.e. spelling, and the grader folds it; not a register issue.

judge_v1.note: تو here is the MSA/lexical noun (immediacy, the very moment), the base of the adverbial تَوًّا 'straightaway' used in standard writing. reference.note: Deliberately checked before calling this a Gulf tell: §1.1 lists توه (the standalone Gulf adverb 'just now'), and the MSA column of that same row gives للتو — which is لـ + this very noun. So تَوّ 'immediacy' is MSA by the programme's own reckoning (لتوّه, توًّا), and the gloss here is exactly that MSA abstract-noun sense, not the adverb. Residual doubt is only that a frequency count over a mixed corpus could have counted dialect توّ; the entry as written is MSA.

judge_v2.note: سنوات is the MSA plural of سنة; nothing dialectal in form or sense.

judge_v2.note: مانع is the MSA active participle of منع and the common noun 'objection, impediment' (لا مانع). The gloss's participial reading is MSA; rank 755 is plausible for the word as a whole.

judge_v1.note: ساعات is the MSA plural of ساعة and is glossed as exactly that. Egyptian uses ساعات adverbially for 'sometimes', but that sense is not what is glossed here, so it is not a tell.

judge_v2.note: ساعات is the MSA plural of ساعة. Egyptian uses the same string adverbially for 'sometimes', but the gloss names the plain MSA plural, which is common enough to earn rank 760 on its own — the rank does not need the dialect sense.

reference.note: MSA broken plural of ساعة. Checked against the non-tell logic deliberately: Egyptian uses ساعات adverbially for 'sometimes', but that dialect sense is not what is glossed here and the plural noun is ordinary MSA, so it is a non-tell in this item. Relation-only gloss again — a definitions-pass item.

judge_v1.note: كِفاية 'sufficiency, competence' is the MSA verbal noun of كفى and is glossed in that sense. The Egyptian interjection كفاية 'enough!' is a different use and is not what is being glossed.

judge_v2.note: كفاية is an MSA verbal noun, 'sufficiency', current in press phrases such as فرض كفاية and حد الكفاية. Egyptian كفاية 'enough!' is a homograph, but per the rank test the gloss names a genuine and reasonably common MSA sense, so the count is plausibly earned and the entry stands.

reference.note: The one item I weighed hardest for a dialect call and cleared. Egyptian/Levantine كفاية! 'enough!' is a homograph, but كفاية 'sufficiency, competence' is common, productive MSA — عدم كفاية الأدلة, فرض كفاية, الكفاية الذاتية — so this is not the §4.2 retire pattern where a dialect entry is glossed as a RARE MSA homograph (مش 'to suck the marrow', وين 'black grape'). The word is an MSA word and the gloss is its MSA sense, so Q2 is a yes. Only caveat worth passing to a reviewer: if the rank-775 count proves to be driven by the dialect interjection, the frequency entry (not the gloss) is what would need retiring.

judge_v1.note: ذاك is a standard MSA far demonstrative (ذلك is more frequent in press, ذاك is still ordinary written Arabic). It is not the Egyptian ده/دي family and not archaic.

judge_v2.note: ذاك is a standard MSA far demonstrative, the shorter counterpart of ذلك, and is still used productively in written Arabic — not archaic, and not the Levantine هاد/هداك series.

reference.note: ذاك is a standard MSA demonstrative in the ذا/ذاك/ذلك series and the gloss names it as such. The dialect demonstratives on the §1.1 list are ده/دي/دول (Egyptian) and هاد/هاي/هدول (Levantine); ذاك is none of them and is not post-nominal here.

judge_v1.note: معروف is the MSA passive participle of عرف, 'known, well-known' (also the noun 'kindness, favour'). No dialect form.

judge_v2.note: معروف is the MSA passive participle of عرف, 'known, well-known', plus the noun 'a favour, kindness'. Nothing dialectal; rank 825 is earned by the MSA word.

reference.note: Passive participle of عرف; 'known, recognized' is plain MSA. The noun معروف 'kindness, good' (الأمر بالمعروف) is also MSA. Dialect اعمل معروف 'do me a favour' uses the same MSA word and is not a tell.

judge_v1.note: ورق is MSA, the collective 'leaves/foliage' and 'paper'. The gloss gives the foliage sense, which is standard; no register issue.

judge_v2.note: ورق is MSA. 'Foliage, leaves' (ورق الشجر) is a true MSA sense, though the bulk of rank 830 is likely the 'paper' sense the gloss omits — a completeness issue for the definitions pass, not register.

reference.note: ورق is MSA and 'leaves, foliage' (ورق الشجر) is a genuine MSA sense, so Q2 is a yes. Non-register note: 'paper' is the dominant modern sense at this frequency, so the gloss leads with the secondary one — a gloss-accuracy item for the vocabulary pass.

judge_v1.note: The headword غرض is plain MSA; the usual modern sense is 'purpose, aim, objective'. The English gloss instead gives the rare verb غَرِضَ 'to be vexed/bored', which is a dictionary-deep sense, not a register problem in the Arabic — flagging it for the definition pass, not for a register rewrite.

judge_v2.note: The gloss gives the rare verb غَرِضَ 'to be vexed, distressed', which cannot have earned rank 835; that count belongs to the noun غَرَض 'purpose, aim, objective', ubiquitous in MSA prose. Crucially the homograph carrying the rank is itself MSA, not a dialect word, so the retire rule does not apply — this is a gloss pointing at the wrong sense of an MSA headword, and the fix belongs to the definitions pass.

reference.note: Headword is MSA; the GLOSS is the defect, and it is archaic rather than dialect. غَرِضَ 'to be vexed, weary, disgusted' is a literary/Classical verb that MSA press does not use productively, and the frequency row tags the entry 'verb' on that basis. At rank 835 the count is the very common noun غَرَض 'purpose, aim, objective' (الغرض من, أغراض). This is the §1.4 dictionary-dump pattern — a lexicon's archaic sense attached to a common modern word — and the fix is the plain MSA gloss 'purpose, aim, objective; object', with the POS corrected to noun. Confidence is held at 0.6 because Wehr still lists the verb, so a reviewer could defend it as marginal-but-modern; the surface form itself needs no rewrite, which is why the msa field repeats the headword unchanged. meaning_kept is false because the proposed fix deliberately replaces the glossed sense.

judge_v1.note: هنا 'here' is MSA and shared with the dialects; sharing is not a dialect tell. The Levantine forms would be هون/هاد, which do not appear.

judge_v2.note: هنا is the MSA locative adverb 'here'. Shared with the dialects, but fully standard — the dialect-only items would be وين/فين and their kin, not هنا.

judge_v1.note: Vocative يا أيها الطلاب is the standard MSA address form, not one of the archaic نداء particles (أيا، هيا، وا). Plural imperative انتبهوا is MSA.

judge_v2.note: يا أيها الطلاب is the ordinary MSA vocative used in speeches and textbooks, not a حرف نداء archaism (أيا، هيا، وا would be).

reference.note: يا أيها الطلاب — the ordinary MSA vocative. Checked against §1.4's 'hurf nida' archaisms', which are أيا/هيا/وا, not يا. Imperative انتبهوا and the accusative adverb جيدًا are plain MSA.

judge_v1.note: يا أيها الناس is live MSA oratory and press usage; that it also occurs in the Qurʾan does not make it archaic vocabulary in an everyday sentence.

judge_v2.note: يا أيها الناس — oratorical but current MSA; يا with أيها is the standard vocative, so no archaism.

reference.note: يا أيها الناس is Qur'anic in origin, so Q5 has to be asked deliberately — and the answer is that MSA press, speeches and quoted oratory use it constantly, so it is not 'archaic where MSA press would not be'. اسمعوا كلامي is unremarkable MSA. judge_v1.note: The visible frame (والله ... على تحقيق هدفي) is MSA; the item is classical because of the form it elicits. evidence: لأعملنّ (the energic the blank elicits: 'I shall certainly work')
judge_v2.msa: والله سأعمل بالتأكيد على تحقيق هدفي.
judge_v2.note: The visible words are MSA; what makes this classical is the target answer. Oath + lam of emphasis + نون التوكيد (لأعملنّ) is the energic, which the rules list as a form MSA no longer uses productively. Plain press register is سأعمل بالتأكيد. Confidence held at the reviewer line because the energic sits in the blank rather than in the text: a human should confirm the answer key, and decide whether a drill whose point is teaching نون التوكيد is exempt.

reference.note: والله لأعملنَّ على تحقيق هدفي — the heavy energetic nun after the lam of an oath, which is precisely what point 37 teaches (its explanation gives واللهِ لأنجَحَنَّ). Genuine tension: §1.4 lists energic forms under classical, so a second reviewer could file this classical. I do not, because §6 Q5's operative test is whether MSA press would use it, and the oath + لـ + ـنَّ is the one environment where MSA still writes the energetic productively — quoted vows, editorials, political rhetoric. The light energetic ـَنْ would get a different answer from me. Decision: keep, do not rewrite; rewriting to plain press register would delete the grammar point.

Plain MSA press register is سأقول. Lower confidence than the previous item because there is no oath particle forcing the energic — the key may already be سأقول, so a reviewer should check it.

evidence: لأقولنّ (the energic the blank elicits: 'I will certainly tell')
judge_v2.msa: سأقول الحقيقة بالتأكيد مهما كان الثمن.
judge_v2.note: Same case as ar-drill-37-2 and barer: lam + نون التوكيد (لأقولنّ) with no preceding oath is literary/classical rather than press MSA. مهما كان الثمن is fine MSA and is kept. Low confidence for the same reason — the flagged form is in the answer key, not the displayed text, so route to a human together with its sibling.

reference.note: لأقولنَّ الحقيقة مهما كان الثمن — the same heavy energetic as i=18, but with the oath elided (lam of the answer to a suppressed oath) rather than stated. That is a step further from press usage than the والله version, and it is where I would genuinely want a second Arabic reader: §1.4 would call the energetic archaic, while the construction is live in MSA rhetoric and is the drill's whole teaching point. مهما كان الثمن is an ordinary MSA idiom and nothing else in the sentence is at issue. Routing to a human per §3.1 rather than guessing; if a reviewer rules it in, i=18 goes with it, and if out, both go together.

evidence: يا + (أيتها) + السيدة is the ordinary MSA vocative with a definite noun, not an archaic نداء particle (أيا/هيا/وا)
تفضلي is the standard MSA feminine-singular courtesy imperative
بالجلوس is بـ + a NOUN, i.e. the preposition, not a b-imperfect
judge_v1.note: Plain MSA courtesy formula. The only ب in the line attaches to a noun (الجلوس), so it is the preposition, not the dialect b-imperfect.

judge_v2.note: Vocative with يا + (أيتها) + definite noun is ordinary MSA, not a نداء archaism. بالجلوس is بـ before a NOUN, i.e. the preposition 'with/by', not the b-imperfect. تفضلي is the standard MSA feminine imperative of courtesy.

reference.note: Filled: يا أيتها السيدة، تفضلي بالجلوس. The formal vocative يا + أيتها + definite feminine noun is the MSA pattern the point teaches, and تفضلي بالجلوس is ordinary courteous MSA. Checked against the §1.4 'حرف نداء archaism' line explicitly: the archaisms are أيا/هيا/وا, not يا أيتها, which is current formal MSA. Transliteration follows MSA (yā ayyatuhā as-sayyida).

evidence: لَـ prefixed to the answer slot is the lām of oath/emphasis, which in this pattern requires the energic نون التوكيد (لَأُنجِزَنَّ)
the gloss 'I shall certainly finish' matches the energic, not a plain future
judge_v1.note: No dialect anywhere; the register issue is the energic نون التوكيد, which press-register MSA does not form productively (it survives mainly in fixed oaths). Flagged per the rule that energic forms are classical — a reviewer may well keep it, since this drill appears to teach نون التوكيد on purpose; if kept, it should be labelled a classical/emphatic construction rather than everyday MSA.

judge_v2.note: The لام التوكيد prefix plus the translation 'I shall certainly' pins the blank to an energic form (لأنهيَنَّ). The prompt lists energic forms as classical/archaic, so the fix is plain MSA press register: future سـ plus an adverb of emphasis (حتمًا / بالتأكيد). No dialect anywhere; a reviewer who wants to keep نون التوكيد should at least label the drill as rhetorical/Classical.

reference.note: Genuine second-opinion case. §1.4 names energic نون التوكيد among forms MSA no longer uses productively, yet grammar point 37 is titled 'النداء والتوكيد بالنون' at C1 and exists to teach exactly this — so a 'classical' verdict here would condemn the point, not the row. Against that: the form is alive in MSA oaths and emphatic promises, and لام القسم with an elided oath is regular. The weak spot is the pairing — an oath-strength energic on finishing homework before bed is a context no MSA writer would choose, and this drill is the only one of the three energic drills with no oath present (37-2 has والله). Restoring the oath fixes the naturalness without touching the taught form; a reviewer should rule on whether energics stay in scope at all.

evidence: the line is Qurʾān 1:5 verbatim (إياك نعبد وإياك نستعين), a liturgical quotation rather than a composed sentence
the fronted object pronoun إياك itself is ordinary productive MSA (cf. إياك أعني)
judge_v1.note: Below 0.7 on purpose — wants a reviewer. Every word and the إياك-fronting are MSA, so this is not a dialect or vocabulary problem; the concern is only that the drill sentence is a scriptural verse, which reads as devotional register rather than news/textbook register. The suggested rewrite keeps the drill's grammar point (fronted إياك) but changes 'worship' to 'thank', so the meaning is not preserved; keeping the verse and labelling it a quotation is an equally defensible call.

judge_v2.note: This is Qurʾan 1:5 verbatim (إياك نعبد وإياك نستعين). The individual pieces are MSA — إيا+pronoun fronting is productive, and نستعين is current — so the flag is the citation, not the grammar: the sentence's register is liturgical, not press. Its meaning is the verse, so there is nothing to rewrite; replace the example with a neutral sentence teaching the same fronted object, e.g. إياك نشكر على مساعدتك. Low confidence on purpose — routes to a human, who may reasonably keep a famous verse.

reference.note: Checklist steps 2 and 3 pass — every word is MSA and object fronting with إيا- is standard MSA syntax — but step 5 fails: the sentence is Qurʾān 1:5 verbatim (al-Fātiḥa), and MSA press would not write it outside quotation. The defect is the choice of sentence, not the grammar point. The meaning ('You alone we worship') exists only in the religious register, so per §4.1 it should be replaced rather than 'translated' into MSA; the replacement above keeps the answer إياك and the fronted-object teaching point but not the meaning, hence meaning_kept false. Note the same point's explanation also uses this verse as its example — worth fixing in the same pass.

judge_v2.note: The أمّا … فـ correlative, textbook MSA. معلمون is on the allowed مدرِّس/معلِّم variation list.

stratum: point:The definite article ال — sun and moon letters
text: **ال** attaches to the noun: بيت (a house) → البيت (the house).  Before 'sun letters' (ت، د، س، ش، ص، ن…) the ل assimilates in speech: الشارع sounds ash-shāriʿ, not al-shāriʿ. Before 'moon letters' (ب، ك، م، ق…) the ل is pronounced: القمر = al-qamar.  Writing never changes — only the sound.

evidence: the romanisations given (ash-shāriʿ, al-qamar) keep MSA ق as q, the opposite of the ق→ء/g dialect tell

judge_v2.note: Sun/moon-letter assimilation described for MSA pronunciation (ash-shāriʿ vs al-qamar). Describing pronunciation is not spelling it out dialectally — no ق→g/ء, ث→ت or ذ→د substitution is taught.

reference.note: Sun/moon letter assimilation described for MSA, and the transliterations follow MSA pronunciation as §4.4 requires: al-qamar keeps q for ق, ash-shāriʿ keeps ʿ for ع — no g for ج and no glottal stop for ق. Examples الشارع/القمر are MSA.
